To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
plants have an adaptive developmental response that reduces the density of their stomatal pores following bacterial infection.
plants respond to bacterial infection with a systemic developmental signal that reduces stomatal density.
plants have evolved a developmental response to pathogen attack.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and function of stomata in Arabidopsis thalia.
understanding the mechanisms that control plant development in the face of infection.
the interaction between plant and pathogen, and the mechanisms that plants use to defend themselves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first report of a long-term stomatal response to a pathogen, and this response is systemic and is mediated by salicylic acid.

the bacterial pathogen P. syringae causes the formation of fewer stomata on new leaves, which is mediated by a systemic response involving the phytohornsone SA, and that this effect reduces the potential for future P. syringa infections.
the plant immune system can influence leaf development to reduce stomatal density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bacterial infection systemically suppress stomatal density.
bacterial pathogens can induce systemic suppression of stomata development in leaves that develop after the initial infection.

the plant pathogen, Pseudomonas syringe pv. tomato DC3000, can induce a systemic signal that reduces the density of the stomata on new leaves, and this is mediated by the salicylic acid signalling pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the plant immune system is not only capable of restricting the entry of pathogens via stomatal pores but can also alter development to reduce future stomatal density, thus reducing the potential for future infections.

the plant immune system is not only able to respond to pathogen infection in the local area, but it also has the ability to respond systemically to the infection, thus providing a second level of defence against pathogens.
plants have a second response to pathogen attack, in addition to stomatal closure, to reduce stomatal density.
